newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikko says to revise earnings forecast if needed.
newsitem.headline: Nikko says to revise earnings forecast if needed.

text.p: Nikko Securities Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it may revise its earnings forecast for the first half of 1996/97 to end September 30, if needed.
However, a Nikko official dismissed as speculative a report by the Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily that Nikko's half-year parent current profit was expected to be about 20 billion yen.
"Whether we revise our forecast or not depends on business conditions in September," the official said.
Nikko in May forecast its half-year parent current profit at 38 billion yen against an actual profit of 25.5 billion a year earlier.

"We had good earnings in the first quarter (of 1996/97) as average daily turnover (on the Tokyo stock market) was in line with our expectations at around 500 billion yen," the official said. "But in August, both stock and bond markets did not move much, and we don't know how the markets will be this month."
In July, average turnover value on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) was 318 billion yen a day, and in August it was about 289 billion yen a day, exchange data showed.
Under the rules of the TSE, a firm must revise its earnings forecast if its net or current profits are up or down 30 percent or more from its earlier earnings forecast.
